excerpt: Tara AI (Tara Intelligence) built an AI-assisted product management and sprint planning tool for software teams. Founders, YC history, funding, current status and alternatives.
content:
Tara AI, listed here as Tara Intelligence, made software for planning and tracking engineering work. TechCrunch described it in 2019 as a machine-learning platform that helps companies scope software projects, predict the tasks and engineering resources they need, and monitor progress, working alongside tools such as Jira and Slack. By early 2023 its website, as preserved by the Internet Archive, pitched it as a way to define, plan and track mission-critical product updates, with requirements, sprints, task tracking, docs and stand-ups in one place.

The company was founded by Iba Masood, its CEO, and Syed Ahmed. In a Y Combinator interview, Masood explained that the company first went through YC in the Winter 2015 batch with a careers platform for new graduates (known as Gradberry), grew out of research into analysing programmers' GitHub commits, and pivoted to product management, launching that product in 2017. TechCrunch reported that the founders relocated to Boston and that early customers included Cisco and Orange Silicon Valley, with about three-quarters of users non-technical.

Funding was modest. Masood told YC the company raised roughly $200,000 after YC and about $2.8 million after the pivot, announced as a seed round of around $3 million. In July 2019 it raised a $10 million Series A led by Aspect Ventures, with the Slack Fund, Y Combinator and Moment Ventures taking part, TechCrunch reported.

Current status: when we checked in October 2026, tara.ai no longer showed the product; it redirected to a domain parking page. We found no announcement of a shutdown or acquisition, so treat the product as unavailable unless the company says otherwise. Teams looking for a similar tool should consider the alternatives below.

This page is research, not a review. We have not used Tara AI; facts come from the pages under Sources.
